title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 8
preview: Maddox tried to tank and won by 50, Brad's backup quarterback was a wide receiver, Drew cried over Pollard and then traded him, and the Commish joined the Democratic Socialists of America. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Wow, that just happened. What's next? Week 7 gave us a 50-point beatdown, a veto fight, a trade that came back for a second try, and a quarterback room run by a wide receiver. Week 8 kicks off Thursday, with first place against second. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real Sleeper data: Week 7 results and lineups, transactions through Tuesday Oct 27 at 8:34 PM ET, and Week 8 matchups. "This week" lines stick to matchups, current records, head-to-head streaks, trades, and this week's storylines. Streaks are head-to-head only. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: Two weeks ago Maddox swore he'd throw the rest of the season if Shedeur ever came back. The Commish put Shedeur back Saturday, Maddox cut him in under an hour, and then he went out and beat Mike by 50. Worst tank job I've ever seen. The man tried to throw a game and threw a perfect game instead. Most guys threaten to quit and then quit. Maddox threatens to quit like a guy who keeps announcing he's leaving the party and is somehow DJing it now. Three straight, first place. Somebody tell him the threat was supposed to hurt *him*.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill: 11-2-1 against 11-3, first against second, three straight against five straight. The matchup of the century, between one man who threatened to throw his season and one who couldn't lose if he tried.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 9, in a game Brian swears he wasn't watching.

entries.roast: Brian started Bryce Young. Bryce Young gave him 4.05. Brian won by 18. I think he's tried to lose. I'm not sure he knows how. Five straight head-to-head wins, the longest streak of the dynasty era. Somebody asked Brian his secret and he said he sets a lineup and then the other guy loses. I set a lineup once. It's still losing. Next up: first place against second, the matchup of the century. This week the Bat-Signal goes up over first place. On the other side is a man who threatened to burn down his own season over a backup quarterback. Some men just want to watch the world burn. Brian just wants to watch it from 11-3.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox: five straight head-to-head wins, the longest streak of the dynasty era, against the only team with a better record. Somebody finally has to try.
entries.prediction: Brian loses by 9 and nobody, including Brian, is sure he was trying.

entries.roast: Kyle put up 166.45, the best score in the league! Two straight wins! And he's 7-7. Fourth in the league in points and sitting at .500, like the guy who brings the best dish to the potluck and still goes home hungry. Now look at this lineup. Kyle's a Patriots fan to his CORE. Gronk Nation! And Sunday he benched the Patriots. Rhamondre Stevenson scored 24 on his bench. The Patriots defense sat on his bench too and scored negative 0.8. NEGATIVE! So who'd he start? The Browns defense. The BROWNS! Kyle finally cheated on New England, and it was the best decision he made all week. Meanwhile Michigan lost to Indiana 13-6 in overtime, and Kyle enjoyed that more than his own 166.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado: 7-7 with two straight wins against 4-10 and dead last. Kyle has the hot hand, and Taylor has the flex problem.

entries.roast: Five straight losses, the longest skid of the dynasty era, so Brad did what every man in a slump does: he went to the sportsbook. UCLA minus 40.5 against Michigan State, a hundred to win fourteen hundred. UCLA won by 18. Taylor asked if he made the bet, and Brad went quiet, which in gambling is what we call a yes. Then Sunday came: Allen on bye, Simpson out, and Brad's quarterback was Xavier Worthy, a wide receiver, for 4.1. Brad lost by 18. Only Brad could stand on 18 twice in one weekend and lose to the house both times. Brad doesn't have a gambling problem. He has a losing problem, and gambling is just the one that charges a fee. Next up is the Commish, the game Brad said he had circled. He also circled UCLA.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer: five straight losses against four straight losses. Somebody's streak ends Sunday, and for once Brad doesn't have to cover 40.5.
entries.prediction: Brad loses by 15 and goes quiet when anyone asks about it.

entries.roast: Oh, NOW the Commish cares about fairness? Tuesday he looks at Drew and Mike's trade and says it's "way too lopsided." Lopsided! Sunday this guy starts Tyler Shough at superflex over Bo Nix. Sleeper had Nix four points higher. The app TOLD you! Nix drops 28.4 on the bench, Shough gives you 16.1, you lose to Kasik. Second-highest scorer in the league and still on a four-game skid. You want lopsided, Ryan? Look at your own lineup! Then he's got the stones to stick his nose in somebody else's deal. Congratulations, comrade: the Commish is now a card-carrying member of the Democratic Socialists of America. Free market for thee, five-year plan for me. And word is the next item on the party agenda is redistribution.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser: five-and-nine on a four-game skid against the era's longest skid at five. Brad said he had this one circled. The Commish just joined the Democratic Socialists of America, so a loss this week gets redistributed.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 15, then vetoes the result for being lopsided.

entries.roast: Drew sat there Sunday CRYING. His words: "I'm crying with Tony Pollard on my bench." Pollard goes for 39.5 and three touchdowns, a career day, and Drew watches the whole thing from the bench like a guy watching his ex win the lottery on the Jumbotron. So what does he do with all those tears? Two days later he ships Pollard to Mike! You don't trade the guy who made you cry, Drew. You START him! But hey, he got Chuba Hubbard back, 11 days after trading him away. He threw a boomerang and caught it with his face. And now Drew's sitting on four 2027 second-rounders like a man with a pocketful of raffle tickets. Bad news, man. The Commish read the Democratic Socialists' handbook. Those seconds are getting redistributed.
entries.this_week: vs Nicholas Kasik: 6-8 with Hubbard back for a second tour, Mike Evans and Chase Brown fresh off the truck, and four 2027 seconds the Commish is eyeing for redistribution.
entries.prediction: Drew loses by 12 and offers Kasik a second-rounder before the final whistle.

entries.roast: Mike lost to Maddox by 50.45, the worst beating of the week, so he's our guest of honor at the podium. Mike waited all season for Josh Jacobs to finally suit up. All season! Jacobs finally suits up, puts up 20.1... on Mike's bench. That's waiting six months for a table at the best steakhouse in town and then ordering the salad. Then Mike goes on a free-market speech, "Shooters shoot," and shoots two first-round picks out the door for Pollard and Puka. And that Chuba Hubbard thing? Mike checked Hubbard out for 11 days and returned him with a 2027 and a 2029 first as the late fee.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo: 8-6 with two fewer first-round picks and Pollard and Puka on the roster, against a 5-9 team that just won by 44.6. Shooters shoot.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 20, with Pollard starting this time.

entries.roast: Kasik beat the Commish by 22.8, and Jameson Williams put up 26.1 to do it. So naturally, as a trained legal professional, he traded him. Jameson Williams and a third to Taylor for Christian Watson, who scored 10.7 for Taylor that same week. Here's the beautiful part: it went through on the first try. No veto. No pushback. No Commish. Meanwhile Drew and Mike needed a veto, a rewrite and a group-chat referendum, and Kasik closed in one motion because a lawyer drafted the paperwork. "Ryan is pro government intervention," he said, and then he made a deal so clean the government never even heard about it. Then again, Kasik never needed the Commish's blessing. The only Nick whose approval he cares about lives in Boston.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman: 7-7 against 6-8. Kasik closed his trade on the first try, and Drew needed a veto and a rewrite. Sunday finds out whose paperwork was better.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 12 and closes it on the first try.

entries.roast: Taylor's dead last at 4-10 with the lowest score of the week, 102.3. He put Tyler Higbee in the FLEX! The flex is the one spot where you can play anybody, and Michael Wilson and Tyler Allgeier both projected higher. Higbee gave him 3.4. But that's not what Taylor wanted to talk about Tuesday. Taylor wanted to tell the other Nick that a gay bar in Massachusetts was "soft closing." And I gotta ask, man... why do you know that? A man doesn't follow the business news of New England's gay bars unless... you know. I'm not saying Taylor's homophobic. I'm just saying, Taylor, remember when you brought up the gay bar you and Brad went to in Chicago? Unprompted? In the middle of explaining why gay bars are bad?
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano: last place, two straight losses, and a brand-new Jameson Williams. Taylor's on his tenth defense of the season, and he picked up another one on waivers this morning. Kyle isn't playing a team Sunday, he's playing a staffing agency.
entries.prediction: Taylor loses by 25 and blames the flex.

entries.roast: Cardillo's doing great, everybody. 2-0 week, beat Taylor by 44.6, all the way up to 5-9. And who knows, maybe one day Nick will get a job. Thursday night, Luther Burden has about 20 at halftime and Cardillo can't contain himself: "Luther isn't a problem, he's a burden." That's the first time in history anybody has called his own guy a burden as a compliment. Burden finishes with 26.2. Good for him. Then Taylor checked in with Nick about a gay bar in Massachusetts closing. Taylor, he doesn't need a bar. He's already got a Nick.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet: 5-9 and riding a win against 8-6, with Mike trying to forget the 50-point loss. Mike gets his first look at Pollard and Puka, and Cardillo gets to see if a "burden" travels.
entries.prediction: Cardillo loses by 20, and the burden is all his.
